source_key_points: 3 FINDING COMMON GROUND 3.1 The Greatest of All Sameeksha is building her new house.
She feels that the room would look nice if the floor is covered with square tiles of the same size.
She also wants to use as few tiles as possible, and for the length of the tile to be a whole number of feet.
Let us explore how to find the largest square tile that can be used.
For the tiles to fit the breadth of the room exactly, the side of the tile should be a factor of 12.
Similarly, for the tiles to fit the length of the room exactly, the side should be a factor of 16.
So the side of the tile should be a factor of both 12 and 16.
What if Sameeksha did not insist on the length of the tile to be a Try whole number of feet and the length could be a fractional number This of feet?
The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of two or more numbers, is the highest (or greatest) of their common factors.
